question: Does one policy-step sensor staleness worsen motion after straight travel and turning?

method.history: ten time-major frames; delay angular velocity, gravity, joint position and velocity after corruption/scaling; preserve command and previous raw action timing; advance once per policy tick
method.initialization: first available observation repeated at startup/reset; initial sample age 0
method.estimated_velocity_error: same-step pre-action estimate minus pre-action physical truth
method.body_and_joint_states: post-step simulator states; policy action and ROA diagnostics are pre-action
method.hip_target: first two raw actions times 0.25; physical joints resolved by names
method.rms: hip quantities average both components; body roll/pitch RMS uses sum of squared components
method.reset_exclusion: exclude done sample and next 49 samples; differences require consecutive valid steps

limitations: 20 ms is a controlled hypothesis, not measured hardware sensor age.
Uniform sensor staleness does not cover asynchronous sensors, jitter, packet loss, filtering or actual command transport.
One seed, one speed/turn magnitude, nominal plane/mechanics and no push.
No physical incident recording or current deployed-byte evidence; pause hardware reproduction.
No instantaneous physics-substep saturation/contact telemetry; sampled limits cannot prove hardware margin.
No approved convergence or hardware acceptance thresholds.
